chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 62 — The Son of Man Revealed and the Garment of Life
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic or Greek wording has been identified for the Parables. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all sixteen verses: the rulers' recognition of the Chosen One, the enthroned Son of Man's judgment, the removal of those who oppressed his children and chosen ones, and the righteous receiving imperishable garments of life. The witness's titles Chosen One, Son of Man and Son of Woman are retained in their distinct occurrences, as are its severe sword and punishment images. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: Thus the Lord commanded the kings, the mighty, the exalted, and those who dwell upon the earth: ‘Open your eyes and lift up your horns, if you are able to recognize the Chosen One.’
verses.study: Earth's rulers are ordered to look upward and recognize the One whose authority they ignored. Their lifted horns, symbols of strength, are powerless unless joined to true recognition.
crossReferences: Psalm 2:10–12 — rulers are warned to submit to the LORD's anointed
Daniel 7:13–14 — the humanlike ruler receives universal dominion

verses.text: The Lord of Spirits sat upon the throne of His glory, and the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him. The word of his mouth will kill all sinners and all the lawless, and they will perish from before his face.
verses.study: The Chosen One judges by a Spirit-given word rather than by borrowed earthly force. Lawlessness cannot remain before his unveiled presence.
crossReferences: Isaiah 11:2–4 — the Spirit-anointed ruler strikes the wicked with the word of his mouth
2 Thessalonians 2:8 — the lawless one is destroyed by the Lord's breath and appearing

verses.text: On that day all the kings, the mighty, the exalted, and those who possess the dry ground will stand. They will see and recognize that he sits upon the throne of his glory, that the righteous are judged in righteousness before him, and that no empty word is spoken in his presence.
verses.study: Recognition arrives when rulers see the throne and the integrity of its court. Judgment is righteous and speech is purified of emptiness before the Chosen One.
crossReferences: Psalm 9:7–8 — the LORD judges the world with righteousness
Matthew 12:36 — empty words come under judgment

verses.text: Pain will come upon them like a woman in labor, like the anguish of childbirth when her child reaches the mouth of the womb and she suffers in giving birth.
verses.study: Labor pain conveys an unavoidable crisis already reaching completion. The rulers cannot reverse the day now coming forth.
crossReferences: Isaiah 13:8 — judgment seizes people with anguish like childbirth
1 Thessalonians 5:3 — sudden destruction comes like labor pains

verses.text: They will look at one another and be astonished. They will lower their faces, and pain will seize them when they see that Son of Woman sitting upon the throne of his glory.
verses.study: Mutual astonishment replaces royal confidence. The title Son of Woman emphasizes the human identity of the enthroned judge before whom the powerful lower their faces.
crossReferences: Daniel 7:13–14 — one like a son of man approaches the heavenly throne
Revelation 6:15–17 — rulers hide from the face of the enthroned judge

verses.text: The kings, the mighty, and all who possess the earth will glorify, bless and exalt the One who rules everything hidden.
verses.study: Those who controlled visible lands confront the ruler of hidden reality. Their praise confesses a sovereignty deeper than political possession.
crossReferences: Daniel 2:22 — God knows what lies in darkness and reveals hidden things
Philippians 2:10–11 — every ruler finally confesses the Lord

verses.text: For from the beginning the Son of Man was hidden, and the Most High preserved him before His power and revealed him to the chosen.
verses.study: The Son of Man's revelation is not an improvised response to evil. Hidden from the beginning and preserved by the Most High, he is unveiled for the chosen at the appointed time.
crossReferences: Colossians 1:26 — the mystery hidden for ages is revealed to the holy
1 Peter 1:20 — the chosen deliverer is foreknown before the world's foundation and revealed later

verses.text: The assembly of the holy and chosen will be planted, and all the chosen will stand before him on that day.
verses.study: While rulers lose their footing, the chosen assembly is planted and stands. Stability flows from belonging before the revealed Son of Man.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:3–5 — the righteous are planted while the wicked do not stand in judgment
Isaiah 61:3 — the restored are called a planting of the LORD

verses.text: All the kings, the mighty, the exalted, and those who rule the dry ground will fall on their faces before him and worship. They will place their hope in that Son of Man, petition him and ask him for mercy.
verses.study: The rulers' late appeal acknowledges the mercy and authority they formerly refused. Their posture reverses every claim of self-exalting rule.
crossReferences: Psalm 72:9–11 — rulers bow before the righteous king
Revelation 1:7 — those who rejected the coming One see him openly

verses.text: Then the Lord of Spirits will press them to hurry and depart from before His face. Their faces will be filled with shame, and darkness will increase upon them.
verses.study: Their petition does not erase the settled judgment. Shame and darkness now mark those who used earthly power without righteous recognition.
crossReferences: Daniel 12:2 — some awaken to shame and lasting contempt
Matthew 25:30 — the unfaithful are sent into outer darkness

verses.text: The angels of punishment will receive them, so that vengeance may be exacted from those who oppressed his children and his chosen ones.
verses.study: The charge is specific: oppression of those belonging to the Chosen One. Angelic punishment answers violence done to vulnerable children and chosen people.
crossReferences: Luke 18:7–8 — God brings justice for His chosen who cry out
Revelation 6:9–11 — the slain await just vengeance

verses.text: They will become a spectacle for his righteous and chosen ones. They will rejoice over them, because the wrath of the Lord of Spirits rests upon them and the sword of the Lord of Spirits is drunk with them.
verses.study: The severe image portrays the public end of oppression. The righteous rejoice in vindication, not in acquiring the rulers' methods for themselves.
crossReferences: Isaiah 34:5–6 — the LORD's sword is pictured as filled in judgment
Revelation 19:1–2 — heaven rejoices because corrupting violence is judged

verses.text: The righteous and chosen will be saved on that day, and from then on they will no longer see the faces of sinners and the lawless.
verses.study: Salvation includes lasting separation from the oppressive presence that once confronted them. The recurring face of lawlessness is removed from their future.
crossReferences: Psalm 37:9–10 — the wicked disappear while the faithful inherit the land
Revelation 21:27 — nothing unclean enters the restored dwelling

verses.text: The Lord of Spirits will dwell over them. They will dwell with that Son of Man, and they will eat, lie down and rise up with him forever and ever.
verses.study: The chosen receive ordinary life transformed by unending fellowship: eating, resting and rising with the Son of Man beneath the Lord's dwelling presence.
crossReferences: Isaiah 25:6 — the LORD prepares a feast for His people
Luke 22:28–30 — the faithful eat and drink at the appointed king's table
Revelation 21:3 — God's dwelling is with humanity

verses.text: The righteous and chosen have risen from the dry ground, ceased to lower their faces, and put on the garment of life.
verses.study: Resurrection reverses humiliation. Faces once lowered are lifted, and mortal exposure is replaced by life worn like a garment.
crossReferences: Isaiah 61:10 — salvation and righteousness are worn as garments
1 Corinthians 15:53–54 — mortality puts on immortality

verses.text: This will be a garment of life from the Lord of Spirits. Your garments will not wear out, and your glory will not fail before the Lord of Spirits.
verses.study: The final gift is durable because it comes from the Lord. Neither the garment nor the glory of the chosen decays in His presence.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 8:4 — garments preserved from wearing out anticipate divine care
2 Corinthians 5:1–4 — heavenly clothing replaces mortal frailty
Revelation 3:5 — the victorious are clothed in enduring white garments

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 62 stages the public recognition of the Chosen One by rulers who had possessed the earth without acknowledging his authority. Titles shift among Chosen One, Son of Woman and Son of Man, joining heavenly appointment to genuinely human identity.

The judgment is word-governed, Spirit-filled and righteous. Hidden paths and empty speech cannot survive before the throne, while oppression of the Chosen One's children becomes the explicit ground for vengeance.
The rulers' fall contrasts with the chosen assembly being planted. The righteous are saved not merely from punishment but for dwelling, fellowship, food, rest and rising with the Son of Man forever.
The garment of life completes the reversal. Shame, darkness and lowered faces give way to resurrection, imperishable clothing and glory that does not fail before the Lord of Spirits.

crossReferences: Isaiah 11:2–4 — the Spirit-filled judge and the word of his mouth
Daniel 7:13–14 — the humanlike ruler enthroned in glory
Matthew 25:31–32 — the Son of Man judging from the throne
1 Corinthians 15:53–54 — mortality clothed with immortality
Revelation 21:3, 27 — enduring divine dwelling without lawlessness
